### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. coxopodopatellar syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.716)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:11603)

**Proposed mechanism:** TBX4 pathogenic variant (HGVS:c.XXX>Y) —DISRUPTS→ TBX4 (HGNC:11603); TBX4 (HGNC:11603) —DECREASES→ Regulation of chondrocyte differentiation (GO:0002067); Regulation of chondrocyte differentiation (GO:0002067) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoplastic fibula (HP:0008970); Regulation of chondrocyte differentiation (GO:0002067) —LEADS_TO→ Patellar aplasia or hypoplasia (HP:0003025). Pathogenic variants in TBX4 lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting the regulation of chondrocyte differentiation. This disruption affects skeletal development, manifesting as hypoplastic fibula in Mungai-Kibito syndrome and patellar aplasia or hypoplasia in coxopodopatellar syndrome, demonstrating a shared pathway of skeletal development regulation.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in TBX4 with a consistent loss-of-function or haploinsufficiency effect in individuals with Mungai-Kibito syndrome (MONDO:0011054) and coxopodopatellar syndrome (MONDO:0007841) would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if variants in TBX4 are found to cause gain-of-function effects or if mutations in entirely different genes are consistently identified as the sole cause for each disease, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in the coding region of TBX4 in gnomAD that are known to cause these specific phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TBX4 in skeletal development could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both Mungai-Kibito syndrome and coxopodopatellar syndrome, potentially focusing on pathways that modulate chondrocyte differentiation or downstream skeletal signaling.
